description: Gradients of scaled dot-product attention: dq, dk and dv from dO, given q, k, v, the forward output o and its softmax statistics. Its problem space is sdpa_fwd's without the paged form and generate_stats, plus the gradients a forward does not write: dbias and dsink; its ragged form carries the per-batch lengths the forward's compact one leaves out.

heads_kv.description: KV head count. Equal to heads is MHA, 1 is MQA, anything between is GQA.

head_dim.description: Per-head width. 8 and up: narrower is not an attention head, and without a range the search spends half its draws below 16. Up to 576 for absorbed MLA's Q and K (value_head_dim mla); a V as wide as Q stays at 512 or less. The common values are the two MLA widths, beside the regime buckets 64, 128 and 256, so the search is seeded where an MLA combination can hold a problem: the constraints admit no other width there, which a walk does not find by stepping.

value_head_dim.description: Width of V, and so of O (and dO, dV), against Q and K's head_dim. same (default): equal, as nearly every model has. mla: 64 narrower, DeepSeek's multi-head latent attention, whose Q and K carry a 64-wide rotary part that V does not -- 192/128 in prefill and training, 576/512 with the latent absorbed in decode. hipDNN requires only Q and K's last dims to agree (SdpaFwdNode Rule 2, SdpaBwdNode Rule 3; O, dO and dV take V's), and ASM SDPA and FlyDSL ship kernels for such pairs. The backward declares both pairs, as the forward does: 192/128 is the training pair, and 576/512 is the backward of the absorbed decode. No training step runs the absorbed form, but converted inference graphs reach the backward in it (dnn-benchmarking's SDPA OOTB corpus, 2026-11-24, kimi_k3 generation at 576/512, which no engine served), so a model needs data there too. The mla pairs are pinned on purpose to DeepSeek's 192/128 and 576/512, and other unequal Q/K and V widths (128/64, 129/65, or any V an engine's pair buckets take) are deliberately left out of the corpus, so UHD has no data for them. The deepseek_v3_mla_prefill and mla_absorbed_decode archetypes anchor them.

alignment.description: Which corner the diagonal is anchored at. Only a distinct problem where the mask is causal or windowed and seqlen_q < seqlen_k; the constraint below pins it to top_left everywhere else, so the sweep does not spend half its budget measuring each shape twice. An engine that serves one anchor and refuses the other is removed from a comparison by the corpus rather than by a measurement, which is why this is a declared axis rather than a fixed choice.

dtype.description: Element type of Q, K, V, O, dO and the gradients dQ, dK and dV, all one type; the softmax statistics the forward saved are fp32. The backward declares no fp8: hipDNN's SdpaBackwardAttributes has no descale, scale or amax operand to carry the dequantization an fp8 input needs, and none of the references or engines takes one; the "// types" note under graph_builder has the evidence. sdpa_fwd declares the fp8 encodings.

layout.description: Memory order of the attention operands; dims stay (B, H, S, D) and the order lives in the strides. bshd (default) is token-major for every tensor, [S*H*D, D, H*D, 1]. bhsd is head-major for every tensor, [H*S*D, S*D, D, 1]. kv_bhsd is the decode KV cache: Q, O (and dO, dQ) token-major and K, V (and dK, dV) head-major. Statistics stay row-major. Which layouts an engine serves differs a great deal, so this is a declared axis and the engine oracle filters it; it is not part of the regime label. Extents of 1 make layouts alias (with seqlen_q 1 and heads 1, kv_bhsd is bhsd; with seqlen_k 1 and heads_kv 1, it is bshd), so the constraints below leave kv_bhsd out of those points: the same graph would otherwise be listed under two layouts. sbhd is sequence-major, Megatron's [S, B, H, D]: [H*D, D, B*H*D, 1] for every tensor; with one batch, or one row in both sequences, it is bshd, so it is declared only where batch > 1 and a sequence is longer than 1. qkv_packed: Q, K and V (and dQ, dK, dV) are views of one fused QKV projection, a row of heads*head_dim + heads_kv*head_dim + heads_kv*value width per token, so each has [S*R, W, R, 1] for its own width W; O and dO stay token-major. A fused QKV projection is self-attention, so qkv_packed is declared only with seqlen_q == seqlen_k. The ragged form packs tokens through offset tensors and needs token-major strides, so it is declared only with the token-major bshd and qkv_packed.

scale.description: The attention scale. inv_sqrt_d (default) is 1/sqrt(head_dim). unit is 1.0, a model that folds the scale into Q. jitter is 1/sqrt(head_dim) times (0.5 + 0.15 * r) for r = (seqlen_k + 3*seqlen_q + batch + head_dim) % 13, a deterministic stand-in for an arbitrary scale in [0.5, 2.3] times the standard one. The modulus is 13 so that power-of-two extents, which fill the archetypes, spread over 12 of the 13 residues instead of landing on one, and no residue gives exactly 1 (so jitter is never the inv_sqrt_d graph). Never 0: a zero scale means unset and omits the attribute. It is the stated value only where the form states one: scale_unset states none and scale_tensor passes it as a runtime tensor, so those two take inv_sqrt_d (the constraints below), and one graph is not listed under three scales.

window.description: Sliding window: local_N keeps the N keys ending at the diagonal (left bound N; the right bound is whatever the mask sets, 0 under a causal mask). none (default) has no left bound. The left bound is never 0, which the frontend rejects. The frontend accepts a left bound under any mask, so the window is not tied to a causal mask here; an engine that serves windows only causally is filtered by the oracle. A window with seqlen_q > seqlen_k is excluded: with the diagonal anchored top-left, every query row from seqlen_k + N - 1 on would keep no key at all.

form.description: Which optional attributes and tensors the graph binds (RFC 0019 §6.7, absent is not zero, and §6.8 rule 9: a model must tolerate any optional feature a valid graph leaves unbound). One aspect varies per graph from the plain baseline, so every optional input appears both present and absent without crossing them all. plain states the scale and binds nothing optional; scale_unset leaves the scale unstated; scale_tensor gives it as a pass-by-value tensor; dropout adds Philox dropout with an INT64 seed and offset; padded adds per-batch seq_len_q and seq_len_kv; ragged packs Q, O, dO, dQ and the statistics through one offset tensor and K, V, dK and dV through another, with the per-batch lengths and padding mask beside them (cuDNN's THD backward; the forward's ragged is compact THD, without lengths); bias adds an additive [1, 1, seqlen_q, seqlen_k] bias (attn_mask only: no dbias is written, a fixed mask); dbias adds a learned per-head [1, heads, seqlen_q, seqlen_k] bias and writes its gradient in the same dims (T5, Swin and AlphaFold relative biases); sink binds one FLOAT sink logit per query head, a frozen sink, without its gradient; dsink binds it and writes dSink, [1, heads, 1, 1] FLOAT, as a model that learns its sinks trains (gpt-oss); alibi sets alibi_mask, cuDNN's ALiBi with no tensor (the slopes follow the query head count, SEM-021), declared causal and top-left only, as the references define it. A --model-shapes file with no `q.form` column reads every row as plain; a column left empty in a row is refused. Every form is an even stratum, and the forms are not weighted (unlike layout, scale and window), so the cut to --count takes each form evenly, as far as the first pass holds it. Without --count the forms declared in fewer combinations get fewer graphs: scale_unset and scale_tensor take inv_sqrt_d only and ragged takes the token-major layouts (bshd, qkv_packed) only. --form-floor tops each form up to its count. Interactions: the form decides whether the `scale` facet applies (scale_unset and scale_tensor ignore it, so they are held at inv_sqrt_d) and which `layout` is meaningful (ragged is token-major: bshd and qkv_packed only). Every other pairing with layout, window and scale is a valid graph; an engine that serves only some of them is filtered by the oracle.

// regime_label: The populations a corpus is reported per, as RFC 0019.13 §11.2's regret table needs them.
Phase: decode is one query token against a cache and is memory bound on that cache;
prefill is the whole prompt at once and is compute bound on the score matrix. They are the
same operation and entirely different problems, which is why they are anchored as separate
archetypes rather than as one range over seqlen_q. Cross attention (more queries than keys)
draws its two sequences from different tensors, so it varies independently of the rest --
a causal mask there is anchored top-left, so every query row keeps a key, and the clause
Grouping (mha/gqa/mqa) is the third facet: how many query heads share one KV head decides
how much of the KV cache a wavefront re-reads, which is the whole difference between a
decode that is bandwidth bound and one that is not. It is a label rather than a bucket
because what matters is heads_kv relative to heads, not its magnitude.
// form_label: The optional aspects a graph binds, reported as a facet column of its own and counted by --form-floor.
Not part of the regime label above: forms cross every regime, so joining them in would multiply
the regime names (and break the quotas keyed on them) instead of adding a column.
Each non-plain value is one clause on the declared `form` parameter, so a focused search pins it.
// kernel_catalog: How a descriptor pack's metadata reads back as a point. The pack names its fields whatever
the kernel author named them; this is the only place those spellings appear, so a new pack
vocabulary is a declaration edit rather than a code change. A descriptor missing any mapped
field carries no geometry and contributes nothing -- which is how pointwise_add and the
shipped tiled_attention are excluded without naming them anywhere.
A pack value with no entry under `enums` is skipped and counted, never guessed: a pack in
fp8 read as bf16 would produce a corpus of graphs the engine does not serve, labelled as
`constants` answers for a parameter the pack vocabulary has no field for at all. These
packs record `causal` without recording which corner the diagonal is anchored at, because
every kernel in them anchors it top-left; saying so here is what lets the builder resolve
an argument no descriptor supplies. A parameter mapped under `metadata` is refused here,
so a constant can never overwrite what a descriptor actually said.
// model_shape_defaults: A model-shape CSV written before one of these parameters was declared has no column for it; the file's rows then mean the default named here. Only these: a parameter with no column and no entry here (alignment, generate_stats, ...) is refused, since filling it in would pass off an unrecorded shape as recorded. The pack `constants` above answer for kernel packs and are not used for shape files.

// types: Operands carry the declared dtype; accumulation and the score matrix are fp32. Left to default, compute follows io and every fp16/bf16 graph is uniform half precision, which hip-kernel-provider's SdpaFwdPlanBuilder and SdpaBwdPlanBuilder refuse outright ('compute_data_type must be FLOAT') and the ingestor engines decline at graph_match -- a live-engine corpus then admits nothing, indistinguishable from naming an engine that does not exist. The softmax statistics saved by the forward pass are fp32.

The dtype matrix: fp16, bf16 and fp32, with Q, K, V, O, dO, dQ, dK and dV all in that type, the statistics FLOAT, compute type FLOAT, and mma_core_mode absent (the backward schema has no such field). hipDNN's references register those three and no other backward (SdpaBwdSignatureKey::getPlanBuilders); ASM's backward keys its kernels on bf16 or fp16 over all seven tensors (tryGetDataTypeIdentifier), FlyDSL's on fp16 and bf16, with fp32 for the objects that take it (servedElementBytes), and rocKE has no backward.

No fp8 row, unlike sdpa_fwd. The forward's fp8 graphs carry Descale_Q, Descale_K and Descale_V (and cuDNN's softmax and output scaling), but SdpaBackwardAttributes has none of those fields (sdpa_backward_attributes.fbs), so an fp8 backward graph would hand the raw encodings to a plan with nothing to dequantize them by. The references list it as not supported, blocked on a node that has the fp8 descale, scale and amax fields (SdpaReferenceImplementations.md, 'fp8 backward'), the ASM backward declines FP8 for want of a kernel row (tryGetDataTypeIdentifier), and hipDNN's cuDNN shim fails sdpa_fp8_backward. When the schema gains those fields, the fp8 dtypes are added here as sdpa_fwd declares them, with the descales its builder binds.
graph_builder.// layout: BSHD (the default): dims stay (B, H, S, D) and the layout lives in the strides, token-major, as the shipped bundles lay them out. Not row-major: strides_of would give BHSD, and rocKE's dense kernels take no stride kernargs -- stride_q_tok is baked as Hq*D -- so their matcher (hasBshdStrides) declines every BHSD graph. AITER serves BSHD too, so the default keeps both engines in the contest. The `layout` parameter adds bhsd (head-major, [H*S*D, S*D, D, 1]) and kv_bhsd (Q/O token-major, K/V head-major, the decode KV cache), whose batch stride is BSHD's, so only the head and sequence strides differ; sbhd (Megatron's sequence-major order, batch stride H*D) and qkv_packed (Q, K and V as views of one fused QKV projection row, O token-major). value_head_dim mla narrows V, O (and dO, dV) by 64, so their strides use the value width wherever Q's use head_dim. An engine that serves only some of them is filtered by the oracle, per combination, not by a measurement.
graph_builder.// scale: attnScale is the plain form's stated scale, not left to the schema's optional: rocKE's dense matcher declines a graph with no attn_scale_value (the scale is a required f32 kernarg and guessing 1/sqrt(D) is what it refuses to do), so a corpus that was all scale_unset would empty a rocKE corpus. 1/sqrt(head_dim) is the standard scale and what the shipped bundles carry. The other forms leave it out (scale_unset, scale_tensor) or keep it (the rest), and the live-engine oracle drops the forms an engine refuses, which is how rocKE's corpus stays free of them. The `scale` parameter chooses the stated value for the forms that state one; scale_unset states none and scale_tensor passes the value as a runtime tensor, so a constraint holds the facet at inv_sqrt_d there instead of listing the same graph (or tensors differing only in their default) under three scales.
graph_builder.// form: One optional aspect per graph, everything else as the plain graph has it. The conventions are hipDNN's own: SdpaBwdNode requires seq_len_q and seq_len_kv, INT32 [B, 1, 1, 1], when padding_mask is set (detail::validateIndexTensor, Rule 9); the scale tensor is a single-element pass-by-value tensor (validateScalarParameter, Rule 10b), given as a runtime parameter whose default is the plain form's scale; the bias takes Q's dtype and dims [1, 1, seqlen_q, seqlen_k], row-major (Rule 7: last two dims equal seq_q and seq_kv, or 1), and dbias stays unset; the dbias form's bias is per head, [1, heads, seqlen_q, seqlen_k], and dBias takes its dims, strides and dtype (Rule 12), so a seqlen_k that is not a multiple of 8 gives both a row pitch off 16 bytes, as Swin's 49-token windows do; the sink and dSink are one FLOAT logit per query head, [1, heads, 1, 1] (Rule 15: dSink needs the sink and takes its dtype); alibi binds no tensor. The dropout seed and offset are INT64 [1, 1, 1, 1] device tensors as the test SDK builds the forward's (RaggedSdpaDensifyTestGraphs.hpp withPhiloxDropout); the frontend states no rule for them and no explicit dropout mask is needed, so that one is the test SDK's convention, not a validated one. There is no kernel_catalog here to hold a plain constant. ragged is cuDNN's THD backward: Q, O, dO, dQ and the statistics share one INT32 [B+1, 1, 1, 1] offset tensor and K, V, dK and dV another, each multiplier the tensor's token stride (the statistics packed token-major, [seqlen_q*heads, 1, heads, 1], as the forward writes them), with seq_len_q, seq_len_kv and the padding mask beside them (SdpaBwdNode Rule 9). The lengths are not optional here: FlyDSL's backward, the engine that serves ragged, declines offsets without them (checkVarlen), while the forward's compact THD form (the test SDK's makeVllmGraph) has none. Facet interactions are constraints, not builder guards: `scale` is held at inv_sqrt_d under scale_unset and scale_tensor, `ragged` to the token-major layouts (bshd, qkv_packed), and `alibi` to a causal mask anchored top-left, the only ALiBi the references define (SEM-021: the frontend accepts the others, which no reference or engine computes). Everything else crosses freely (padded, dropout and bias with every layout and window), since the frontend validators, the CPU and GPU references and the engine matchers state those as valid or as an engine-level decline, which the oracle filters.
graph_builder.// let: head_dim_v is V's width, and so O's (and dO's and dV's in the backward): head_dim, or 64 narrower under value_head_dim mla. Named once here; every dims and strides argument reads it as $let.head_dim_v.

archetypes.name: gpt3_175b_prefill

archetypes.name: bert_base_encoder
archetypes.note: bidirectional: an encoder is the uncausal case

archetypes.name: vit_encoder
archetypes.note: patch tokens plus a class token

archetypes.name: head_dim_sweep
archetypes.note: the widths real models use, at square prefill shapes: what the corpus needs to cover head_dim, which the model-pinned archetypes above fix at 64 and 128

archetypes.name: cross_attention
archetypes.note: more queries than keys, from different tensors: diffusion and encoder-decoder attention over a short text or memory sequence. Bidirectional, as such attention is, and causal too: the mask over more queries than keys anchored top-left, where every query row keeps a key, which exploration alone reaches a few times in thousands of graphs

archetypes.name: deepseek_v3_mla_prefill
archetypes.note: multi-head latent attention as it trains, the latent expanded: Q and K 192 wide (128 + the 64-wide rotary part), V 128, one KV head per query head; all 128 heads, or the 16 of a tensor-parallel shard (and DeepSeek-V2-Lite). Kept at its recorded size: the 128-head points need a larger --max-bytes than the default 256 MiB (the smallest, batch 1 at 2048 tokens in fp16, is about 641 MiB), and under the default at most three 16-head points fit (batch 1 and 2 at 2048 tokens, batch 1 at 4096)

archetypes.name: qwen3_next_gqa_d256_prefill
archetypes.source: Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B config.json (16 heads, 2 KV heads, head_dim 256); the 32-head qwen3.5 shapes of dnn-benchmarking's SDPA OOTB corpus (2026-11-24), real-world tier
archetypes.note: grouped-query attention at head_dim 256 and 8 or 16 query heads per KV head, square causal prefill (and training): the head_dim_sweep archetype reaches 256 only with one KV head per query head. 4 of its 24 points fit the default --max-bytes of 256 MiB in fp16; the larger ones need a larger ceiling.

archetypes.name: video_dit_full_attention
archetypes.source: Wan 2.2 A14B (40 heads, head_dim 128) and LTX-2 (32 heads, head_dim 128) full spatio-temporal attention at the token counts of dnn-benchmarking's SDPA OOTB corpus (2026-11-24), real-world tier
archetypes.note: unmasked attention over a whole video latent, one batch of 16384 to 75600 tokens: past the long_context archetype's 32768. Kept at its recorded size: no point fits the default --max-bytes of 256 MiB (the smallest, in fp16, is about 1026 MiB), so a default run reports it never admitted; recorded shapes (--model-shapes) carry these sizes exempt from the ceiling.

archetypes.name: mla_shared_kv_prefill
archetypes.source: DeepSeek-R1 and Kimi-K2 training graphs captured in dnn-benchmarking's SDPA OOTB corpus (2026-11-24) (bwd/captured)
archetypes.note: multi-head latent attention as those training runs record it: every query head against one shared KV head, Q and K 192 wide, V 128; the deepseek_v3_mla_prefill archetype expands the latent to one KV head per query head. 1 of its 4 points fit the default --max-bytes of 256 MiB in fp16; the larger ones need a larger ceiling.

archetypes.name: alibi_causal_lm
archetypes.source: BLOOM-176B (112 heads, head_dim 128) and MPT-7B (32 heads, head_dim 128), causal language models with ALiBi positions; the bloom-176b and mpt-7b model_spec backward graphs of dnn-benchmarking's SDPA OOTB run (2026-11-24, rocm-libraries aa791ab77), which no engine served
archetypes.note: causal self-attention with ALiBi (form alibi) at its trained sizes. No backward engine takes ALiBi today (FlyDSL declines it, MW-12, as do ASM SDPA and rocKE), so an engine-backed run reports this archetype never admitted, declined by the engine: that warning is the coverage gap. 3 of its 12 points fit the default --max-bytes of 256 MiB in fp16, all 12 fit 4 GiB.

archetypes.name: swin_window_relative_bias
archetypes.source: Swin-B (4, 8, 16 and 32 heads by stage, head_dim 32, 7x7 windows) relative position bias, learned per head; the swin-base model_spec backward graph of dnn-benchmarking's SDPA OOTB run (2026-11-24, rocm-libraries aa791ab77), which no engine served
archetypes.note: windowed attention over 49 tokens with a learned per-head bias and its gradient (form dbias), the batch counting every window of every image. A 49-key row is 98 bytes in 16 bits, off the 16-byte pitch FlyDSL's dBias needs (BI-9), so today it is a declined graph. 10 of its 16 points fit the default --max-bytes of 256 MiB in fp16.

archetypes.name: padded_head_dim
archetypes.source: AOTriton's backward test head dims and the sweep tier of dnn-benchmarking's SDPA OOTB run (2026-11-24, rocm-libraries aa791ab77): 71 backward graphs at head dims 59, 111 and 203, dense and padded, none served
archetypes.note: head dims that are not a multiple of 8 at their own compact pitch, so no row is 16-byte aligned. The forward serves them on padded copies (FlyDSL's FlydslSdpaHeadPad.hpp); the backward engines decline them (FlyDSL LY-3 and DT-8, ASM's hdim % 8 rule). Exploration draws such widths but neither the archetypes nor the neighbourhood did, so the declined share went unreported. 117 of its 120 points fit the default --max-bytes of 256 MiB in fp16.

archetypes.name: mla_absorbed_decode
archetypes.source: DeepSeek-V3 and Kimi-K2/K3 absorbed MLA decode (one 576-wide latent KV head, V 512); the kimi_k3 generation backward graph of dnn-benchmarking's SDPA OOTB run (2026-11-24, rocm-libraries aa791ab77) (B128 Hq96, 131072 keys), which no engine served
archetypes.note: the backward of a one-token decode against a long latent cache. No training step runs it, but a converted inference graph reaches the backward in this form; FlyDSL declines a head dim above 512 (DT-4). 28 of its 80 points fit the default --max-bytes of 256 MiB in fp16, 56 fit 4 GiB.

archetypes.name: shared_kv_head_dim_512
archetypes.source: the DeepSeek-V4 training captures (captured-bwd) of dnn-benchmarking's SDPA OOTB run (2026-11-24, rocm-libraries aa791ab77): 64 or 128 query heads over one 512-wide KV head, causal with a 128-key window
archetypes.note: the training counterpart of sdpa_fwd's shared_kv_head_dim_512. At 128 heads and 16384 tokens one head's query slab passes 2 GiB, past the 32-bit offsets FlyDSL's backward addresses (DT-9), and no engine served it; that point needs a --max-bytes above 8 GiB. None of its 16 points fit the default 256 MiB in bf16, 8 fit 4 GiB.

archetypes.name: gpt_oss_sink_training
archetypes.source: gpt-oss-120b and -20b (64 heads, 8 KV heads, head_dim 64, learned attention sinks, a 128-token window on alternate layers); the 45 sink graphs dnn-benchmarking's SDPA OOTB run (2026-11-24, rocm-libraries aa791ab77) could not convert to a backward before SdpaBackwardAttributes took a sink
archetypes.note: causal prefill with learned sinks and their gradient (form dsink), on both the full and the windowed layers. 6 of its 18 points fit the default --max-bytes of 256 MiB in bf16.

// archetypes: Recorded transformer configurations (RFC 0019.13 §12.3). Decode and prefill are the same operation and different problems -- seqlen_q of 1 against a long cache is memory bound, and a square prefill is compute bound -- so each is anchored separately rather than left to a range over seqlen_q.
// neighbourhood: head_dim moves among the widths shipped models use rather than scaling, since an interpolated 100 or 144 is not a configuration anyone ships. seqlen_k mirrors seqlen_q at ratios >= 1, the relation of decoder attention (prefill and append); more queries than keys comes from exploration and the cross attention archetype.
// mixture: Same shares as conv_fwd; see the note there.
